title: Fermion Flavour Sector over Finite Substrate

rows.label: A1
rows.predicate: The Subject's arithmetic: the shell $\Fp$ with its frame, the quadratic extension $K$ with its Frobenius $\sigma$, the split cycle $C_{\p-1}$ with the quarter-turn and the unitary cycle $C_{\p+1}$ with the cube roots of unity, on the shells $\p\equiv5\,(\mathrm{mod}\,12)$.

rows.label: A2
rows.predicate: One generation as the $\mathbf{16}$ of $\SO(10)$: field content, hypercharges, charges, anomaly freedom and $\sin^2\theta_W=3/8$.

rows.label: A3
rows.predicate: The Froggatt--Nielsen flavour mechanism and the Wolfenstein parametrisation.

rows.label: A4
rows.predicate: The Gatto--Sartori--Tonin, Georgi--Jarlskog, and lopsided-$\SU(5)$ textures.

rows.label: A5
rows.predicate: The seesaw mechanism and the renormalisation-group running.

rows.label: A6
rows.predicate: Measured anchors: the two $\Delta m^2$, $M_R$, the charged-lepton and quark masses, $V_{us}$ and the mixing angles; the Koide identity is P1's prediction, not an input.

blocks.title: The constitutive moves: namings, and the theorem that states the generations

rows.label: B1
rows.predicate: Matter is the amplitude matrix of a sector: it is Hermitian over $K$, in the sector's generation basis it is a circulant (C1), and a mass is the square of a generation amplitude, the Born square. Falsifier: a charged-lepton spectrum departing from the circulant Koide form at improved precision (present agreement $6\times10^{-6}$); its prediction row is P1.

rows.label: B2
rows.predicate: The three generations of a sector are one orbit of the generation cycle $C_3$: identical in every gauge number, differing only in mass. The closure of the role ladder gives three generations and no fourth \cite{akhtman2026fields}, and the Frobenius exchanges the two nontrivial characters of the cycle, $\sigma(\omega)=\omega^{2}$. Falsifier: a fourth generation, or two generations differing in any gauge number.
rows.name: generations_one_orbit

rows.label: B3
rows.predicate: The role depths $(0,1,2)$ of the closed ladder are the Froggatt--Nielsen flavour charges: a naming, the Cabibbo band its prediction row (P3, with X3 and X4). Falsifier: a confirmed departure of the Wolfenstein hierarchy from the depth ladder $(0,1,2)$, e.g.\ $V_{us}$ outside the band of the Gatto relation for every phase $\varphi$.

rows.label: B4
rows.predicate: The colour excess of the quark amplitudes is the Georgi--Jarlskog Clebsch $\Nc=3$; the squared amplitudes are the cyclotomic norms $N(1-\zeta_n)$, the theorem C4. The down sector carries the colour-dressed lepton value $0.745$ and has no sharp on-shell test. Falsifier: a quark-to-lepton amplitude ratio departing from the $\Nc=3$ Clebsch at improved precision; its prediction row is P2.

rows.label: B5
rows.predicate: A colourless sector (charged leptons, neutrinos) carries the undressed quarter-turn amplitude $r=\sqrt2$, i.e.\ $Q=2/3$: the one input of the Koide chain (C2). Falsifier: $Q_\ell\neq2/3$ at improved charged-lepton precision; for neutrinos, inverted ordering, a degenerate spectrum, or $\sum m_\nu\gtrsim120$\,meV; its prediction rows are P1 and P5, with X1.

rows.label: C1
rows.predicate: A matrix that commutes with the generation shift is a circulant, and two circulants commute. The eigenvalues of a Hermitian circulant, $\lambda_k=a+b\,\omega^{k}+\sigma(b)\,\omega^{2k}$, lie in the shell, and the Koide form parametrises this spectrum: $Q=\tfrac13+\tfrac23\rho^{2}$ with $\rho^{2}=N(b)/a^{2}$.
rows.source: Prop.~\ref{prop:circulant}\newline \pywit{flavour}{p28012}{C1}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p28012}{C1}; rests on B1, B2 \lean{FRC.Flavour.shift\_commutant, FRC.Flavour.circ\_comm, FRC.Flavour.circ\_dag, FRC.Flavour.hermitian\_circulant\_fixed, FRC.Flavour.circ\_eigen, FRC.Flavour.eigen\_sum, FRC.Flavour.eigen\_sumsq, FRC.Interactions.koide\_parseval}
rows.name: generation_universality_circulant

rows.label: C2
rows.predicate: $Q=2/3\Leftrightarrow r=\sqrt2\Leftrightarrow\rho^2=\tfrac12$ (the equivalence an identity); the value $\rho^2=\tfrac12$ is the naming B5.
rows.name: charge_two_thirds_identity

rows.label: C3
rows.predicate: The leading boundary phase is the framed-rational winding $\delta_{\mathrm{LO}}=\tfrac38-\tfrac13=\tfrac1{24}$ cycle (split-torus boundary $\tfrac38$ minus generation $\tfrac13$; continuum $\pi/12$ [approx]); massless lightest generation.
rows.name: leading_boundary_phase

rows.label: C4
rows.predicate: The squared amplitudes are the cyclotomic norms $N(1-i)=2$, of the split cycle, and $N(1-\omega)=3$, of the unitary cycle. On B5 the first gives $Q=\tfrac23$. The second gives $Q=\tfrac56$, which on the amplitudes $(1,a,e)$ is the quadratic $a^{2}-10a(1+e)+(1+e^{2}-10e)=0$. The down sector is the colour-dressed intermediate.
rows.source: Rem.~\ref{rem:23tori}\newline \pywit{flavour}{p28015}{C4}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p28015}{C4}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p28015}{C4}; rests on B4 \lean{FRC.Flavour.norm\_one\_sub\_i, FRC.Flavour.norm\_one\_sub\_omega, FRC.Flavour.koide\_five\_sixths, FRC.Flavour.koide\_five\_sixths\_quadratic, Flavour.koide\_up\_band}
rows.name: squared_amplitudes_cyclotomic_norms

rows.label: C5
rows.predicate: The cube invariant of a sector is the determinant of its circulant, $a^{3}+b^{3}+c^{3}-3abc$. For a unit $z$ of the unitary cycle with trace $T(z)=z+\sigma(z)$, $T(z^{2})=T(z)^{2}-2$ and $T(z^{3})=T(z)^{3}-3T(z)$. These relate the cube invariants of sectors whose phases stand in the ratios $1:\tfrac12:\tfrac13$. The ratios themselves are not a prediction of this paper: on shell they read $0.46$ and $0.39$ [chart].
rows.name: cube_invariant_trace_relations

rows.label: C6
rows.predicate: The Gatto Cabibbo relation $V_{us}=|\sqrt{m_d/m_s}-e^{i\varphi}\sqrt{m_u/m_c}|$, the phase $\varphi$ a kernel datum ($85^\circ\pm10^\circ$ from the data).
rows.name: gatto_cabibbo_relation

rows.label: C7
rows.predicate: Up-sector doubling $m^u_i\sim(m^d_i)^2$ from the $\mathbf{10}\cdot\mathbf{10}$ Yukawa.
rows.name: up_sector_doubling

rows.label: C8
rows.predicate: Lopsided $M_e=M_d^{\mathsf T}$ splits CKM (small) from PMNS (large); the CKM angle values reduce to the winding kernel and the shared $\sigma$.
rows.name: lopsided_splits_ckm

rows.label: C10
rows.predicate: The matrix $F$ of the characters of $C_3$ diagonalises every circulant. It is trimaximal, $|F_{jk}|^{2}=\tfrac13$, and its invariant is $J(F)=1/(6\sqrt3)$, that is $108\,J^{2}=1$. The generation shift fixes $(1,1,1)$ and fixes no multiple of $(2,-1,-1)$. On the form TM2 (Y4) the relation \eqref{eq:tm2} holds, with $|\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}|=90^\circ$ at maximal atmospheric mixing, and the solar value is $1/(3c_{13}^{2})=0.341$ [chart].
rows.source: \S\ref{sec:cp}\newline \pywit{flavour}{p28021}{C10}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p28021}{C10}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p28021}{C10}; rests on Y4 \lean{FRC.Flavour.protected\_column, FRC.Flavour.trimaximal, FRC.Flavour.jarlskog\_sq, Flavour.jarlskog, Flavour.tm2\_at\_maximal, Flavour.exact\_tm2\_solar}
rows.name: character_matrix_tm2_relation

rows.label: C11
rows.predicate: Circulants are closed under product, transpose and adjugate, so the seesaw of circulants of one basis is a circulant. A symmetric circulant $a\,\mathbb 1+b\,(P+P^{2})$ has the eigenvalues $a+2b$, $a-b$, $a-b$: such a seesaw has two equal masses. With $M_R=c\,m_D$ the seesaw collapses to a multiple of $m_D^{\mathsf T}$.
rows.source: Prop.~\ref{prop:seesaw},\,\ref{prop:transpose}\newline \pywit{flavour}{p28022}{C11}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p28022}{C11}; rests on A5, B1, C1 \lean{FRC.Flavour.circ\_mul, FRC.Flavour.circ\_adj, FRC.Flavour.circ\_transpose, FRC.Flavour.seesaw\_circulant, FRC.Flavour.symmetric\_circulant\_spectrum, FRC.Flavour.transpose\_fixed\_point}
rows.name: seesaw_circulants_koide

rows.label: C11b
rows.predicate: Both orderings solved: on the hypothesis Y5 the signed $r_\nu=\sqrt2$ circulant solves both neutrino orderings exactly, so the boundary branch (Y2) is the sole ordering assumption.
rows.name: both_orderings_solved

rows.label: C12
rows.predicate: The generation $\mathbf{16}$ is the four-chart reflection algebra $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^4)\cong\Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}(\C^5)$, the quarter-turn the fifth direction; projection anchored at $\nu^c=\Lambda^0$.
rows.name: generation_reflection_algebra

blocks.title: What the construction explains: the surplus over the flavour data

rows.label: X1
rows.predicate: \textbf{The Koide ratio} is exactly $2/3$ given the quarter-turn naming B5, the cube-root generation orbit bisected at the quarter-turn ($\rho^2=2^{-1}$), an exact value rather than an unexplained empirical coincidence.
rows.name: koide_ratio_quarter_turn

rows.label: X2
rows.predicate: \textbf{The up-quark Koide value} is $5/6$, the norm $N(1-\omega)=3$ of the unitary cycle against the colourless $N(1-i)=2$. On shell the masses give $Q_u=0.832\pm0.003$ [chart], a ratio where the Standard Model carries no relation at all.
rows.name: up_quark_koide_framed

rows.label: X3
rows.predicate: \textbf{The flavour charges} are the role depths $(0,1,2)$ of the closed primitive-role ladder, derived as the three generative roles rather than assigned to fit the hierarchy.
rows.name: flavour_charges_role_depths

rows.label: X4
rows.predicate: \textbf{The Cabibbo angle} is the Gatto relation $V_{us}=|\sqrt{m_d/m_s}-e^{i\varphi}\sqrt{m_u/m_c}|$ following from the role-depth texture, the leading term at $0.3\%$ and the phase $\varphi$ a kernel datum, so two otherwise-independent observables are tied rather than measured apart.
rows.name: cabibbo_angle_gatto

rows.label: X5
rows.predicate: \textbf{The Georgi--Jarlskog factor} is the colour count $N_c=3$, the $B\!-\!L$ Clebsch of the $\overline{\mathbf{126}}$, not a texture coefficient inserted by hand; its double ratio $9$ against the measured $10.4\pm0.5$ is the open $15\%$ excess of the minimal Clebsch.
rows.name: georgi_jarlskog_colour_count

rows.label: X6
rows.predicate: \textbf{The up-sector doubling} $m^u_i\sim(m^d_i)^2$ is forced by the $\mathbf{10}\cdot\mathbf{10}$ Yukawa, so the steeper up hierarchy is a consequence rather than a separate assumption.
rows.name: up_sector_doubling_forced

rows.label: X7
rows.predicate: \textbf{The electron's extreme lightness} is the quarter-turn boundary: the lightest generation sits where the winding amplitude vanishes, massless at leading order, rather than an anomalously small Yukawa tuned by hand.
rows.name: electron_lightness_quarter_turn

rows.label: X8
rows.predicate: \textbf{The large-lepton, small-quark mixing split} is the lopsided $M_e=M_d^{\mathsf T}$: one off-diagonal feeds the invisible right-handed quark rotation and, transposed, the visible left-handed lepton rotation, so the two mixing matrices are one structure rather than two unrelated ones.
rows.name: lepton_quark_mixing_split

rows.label: X10
rows.predicate: \textbf{The invariant of the character matrix} is maximal: $\mathrm{Im}\,\omega=\sqrt3/2$ gives $J(F)=1/(6\sqrt3)$, the largest value a unitary matrix admits. It is a property of $F$, not of the lepton mixing matrix.
rows.name: character_matrix_invariant

rows.label: X11
rows.predicate: \textbf{The neutrino spectrum} on the hypotheses Y5 and Y2: a near-massless lightest state and $\sum m_\nu\simeq59\,$meV on the normal branch, two parameters fixed by the two splittings rather than three independent neutrino masses.
rows.source: \S\ref{sec:neutrino}\newline \pywit{flavour}{p28035}{X11}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p28035}{X11}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p28035}{X11}; rests on Y2, Y5 \lean{FRC.Flavour.eigen\_sumsq, FRC.Flavour.neutrino\_floor\_brackets, Flavour.neutrino\_floor}

rows.predicate: Charged-lepton Koide $Q_\ell=2/3$ exact on B5 (measured $0.666661\pm0.000007$); $m_e=0.5106$ vs $0.5110$ MeV. Falsifier: a lepton-mass shift of $Q_\ell$ off $2/3$ beyond the $\tau$-mass tolerance.

The relation places the pole charm mass between $1.56$ and $1.76$~GeV, for $m_u$ between $5$~MeV and zero. Falsifier: a pole charm mass outside that band.

blocks.title: Hypotheses: stated ahead of their test

rows.label: Y2
rows.predicate: The drive-invariant boundary branch: the lightest colourless neutrino sits at the quarter-turn zero (as the electron), selecting the normal near-$m_1{=}0$ branch; the sole ordering assumption (C11b), a hypothesis tested by one datum. Falsifier: inverted ordering (P5).

rows.label: Y3
rows.predicate: The commutator invariant of the quark sectors, $J=\det(M_uM_d-M_dM_u)$. The Frobenius negates $J$, and $J$ factors as in \eqref{eq:J} \cite{jarlskog1985}. The hypothesis: $J\neq0$, that is three distinct masses in each sector and a mixing matrix with $q\neq\sigma(q)$. The measured quark mixing matrix fulfils it, $\mathrm{Im}\,q\approx3\times10^{-5}$ [chart]; the paper does not derive the phase (T2). Falsifier: a quark mixing matrix that can be made real.

rows.label: Y4
rows.predicate: The lepton mixing matrix has the form TM2: in the mass basis of the charged leptons the neutrino mass matrix has the eigenvector $(1,1,1)/\sqrt3$, the trivial character of $C_3$, which is then the second column of the mixing matrix. The construction does not derive it. Its tests are the relation \eqref{eq:tm2} and the solar value $\sin^2\theta_{12}=1/(3c_{13}^{2})=0.341$, against the measured $0.3092\pm0.0087$ \cite{juno2026}. Falsifier: a solar angle off the TM2 value, or a pair $(\theta_{23},\delta_{\mathrm{CP}})$ off the relation (P8).

rows.label: Y5
rows.predicate:
The neutrino Koide value: the signed amplitudes $\sqrt{m_{
u,k}}$ of the three neutrino masses have the circulant form with $r_
u=\sqrt2$, that is $Q_
u=2/3$ read on the masses with one negative amplitude. The seesaw does not supply it (C11). Its tests are P5, P6 and P7, with the boundary branch Y2. Falsifier: three measured neutrino masses with $Q_
u
eq2/3$ for either sign of the lightest amplitude.

rows.label: Y6
rows.predicate: The estimate of the reactor angle, $\sin\theta_{13}\simeq\sin\theta_C/\sqrt2=0.159$ (quark--lepton complementarity), against the measured $0.1488\pm0.0019$: $7\,\%$ and five standard deviations high. The estimate does not hold on exact TM2 (Y4), no correction is derived, and it is not a prediction. A derived correction decides it.

B2.name: FRC.Flavour.frobenius_characters
B2.doc: 28:B2 — the Frobenius exchanges the two nontrivial characters of the generation cycle: at `ν = −3` the cube root `ω = −h + h w` has `ω̄ = ω²`.

C1.name: FRC.Flavour.shift_commutant
C1.doc: 28:C1 — a matrix that commutes with the shift is a circulant: `A P = P A` gives `A = circ A₀₀ A₀₁ A₀₂`. The circulants are the commutant of the generation shift.

C1.name: FRC.Flavour.circ_dag
C1.doc: 28:B1, 28:C1 — the conjugate transpose of a circulant is the circulant of the conjugates with the row reversed, so a circulant is Hermitian exactly when `ā = a` and `c = b̄`.

C1.name: FRC.Flavour.hermitian_circulant_fixed
C1.doc: 28:B1, 28:C1 — the eigenvalues of a Hermitian circulant are fixed by the Frobenius. With `ā = a`, a cube root `ω` and `ω̄ = ω²` (`frobenius_characters`), the eigenvalue `λ₁ = a + b ω + b̄ ω²` equals its conjugate: it lies in the shell, and a mass is its square.

C1.name: FRC.Flavour.circ_eigen
C1.doc: 28:C1, 28:X11 — on a cube root `ω² + ω + 1 = 0` the circulant has the eigenvectors `(1, ω, ω²)` and `(1, ω², ω)` with the eigenvalues `λ₁ = a + bω + cω²` and `λ₂ = a + bω² + cω` (the first row gives `λ_k` itself; the second and third rows give `ω^k λ_k` and `ω^{2k} λ_k`); the eigenvector `(1, 1, 1)` has `λ₀ = a + b + c`. Universality makes the amplitude matrix a circulant, and this is its spectrum: the Koide functional form.

C1.name: FRC.Flavour.eigen_sum
C1.doc: 28:C1 — the eigenvalues sum to `3a`: `λ₀ + λ₁ + λ₂ = 3a`.

C1.name: FRC.Flavour.eigen_sumsq
C1.doc: 28:C1, 28:C2, 28:C11b, 28:X11, 28:P5 — the squares of the eigenvalues sum to `3a² + 6bc`: at `c = b̄` this is `3a² + 6 N(b)`, so `Q = Σλ²/(Σλ)² = 1/3 + (2/3) N(b)/a²`, the Koide form with `ρ² = N(b)/a²` (`koide_parseval`).

C1.name: FRC.Interactions.koide_parseval
C1.doc: 00:G16, 27:X10, 27:P8, 28:C1, 28:X1 — Parseval on the cube-root orbit `C₃`: for amplitudes `a₀, a₁, a₂` and `ω` with `ω² + ω + 1 = 0`, `3 Σ a_j² = â₀² + 2 â₁ â₂`, `â₀ = Σ a_j`, `â₁ = a₀ + a₁ω + a₂ω²`, `â₂ = a₀ + a₁ω² + a₂ω` — the Koide form `Q = Σ a_j² / (Σ a_j)² = 1/3 + (2/3)ρ²` with `ρ² = â₁â₂/â₀²`, exact on every shell carrying the root `ω`.

C2.name: FRC.Interactions.koide_extension
C2.doc: 00:G16, 27:X10, 27:P8, 28:C2, 28:X1, 28:P1, on every shell: with `h + h = 1` and `ν = −3`, `ω = −h + h w` has `ω² + ω + 1 = 0`; `â₂ = â̄₁`, so `â₁ â₂ = N(â₁)`; Parseval `3 Σ a_j² = â₀² + 2 N(â₁)`; and `Q = 2/3 ⟺ 2 N(â₁) = â₀²` (`ρ² = 1/2`).

C2.name: FRC.Flavour.eigen_sumsq
C2.doc: 28:C1, 28:C2, 28:C11b, 28:X11, 28:P5 — the squares of the eigenvalues sum to `3a² + 6bc`: at `c = b̄` this is `3a² + 6 N(b)`, so `Q = Σλ²/(Σλ)² = 1/3 + (2/3) N(b)/a²`, the Koide form with `ρ² = N(b)/a²` (`koide_parseval`).

C3.name: FRC.Flavour.quarter_turn_boundary
C3.doc: 28:C3, 28:X7 — the massless generation sits at the quarter-turn diagonal. With `i² = −1`, `ω² + ω + 1 = 0` and `h + h = 1`, the circulant `(a, b, c)` with `b = −h(1 + i) a ω²` and `c = −h(1 − i) a ω` (so `c = b̄` when `a, h` are real, `ī = −i`, `ω̄ = ω²`) has `λ₁ = a + bω + cω² = 0` and `2bc = a²`: the vanishing eigenvalue and the Koide value `Q = 2/3` (`2N(b) = a²`) at once.

C3.name: FRC.Flavour.lo_eigen
C3.doc: 28:C3, 28:X7 — the leading-order spectrum. At the boundary of `quarter_turn_boundary` the two remaining eigenvalues are `λ₀ = a h (3 + s)` and `λ₂ = a h (3 − s)` with `s = i (ω − ω²)`, and `s² = 3`: the square-root masses `(0, 3 − √3, 3 + √3)·ah`, the ratios `m_e : m_μ : m_τ = 0 : (2 − √3)² : 1`.

C3.name: FRC.Flavour.lo_ratio_sq
C3.doc: 28:C3, 28:X7 — with `s² = 3`, `(3 − s)² = (7 − 4s)(3 + s)²`: the leading-order ratio `(λ₂/λ₀)² = m_μ/m_τ` is `7 − 4√3 = (2 − √3)² ≈ 0.0718` (observed `0.0595`).

C3.name: FRC.Flavour.delta_lo
C3.doc: 28:C3 — the leading phase as a cycle fraction: `δ_LO = 3/8 − 1/3 = 1/24`, that is `9 − 8 = 1` over the common denominator `24 = 3 · 8`.

C4.name: FRC.Flavour.norm_one_sub_i
C4.doc: 28:C4, 28:X2, 28:P2, 00:G17 — the quarter-turn norm: `(1 − i)(1 + i) = 2` on every shell with `i² = −1`; the squared amplitude of a colourless sector, `r² = N(1 − i) = 2`, so `Q = 1/3 + r²/6 = 2/3`.

C4.name: FRC.Flavour.norm_one_sub_omega
C4.doc: 28:C4, 28:X2, 28:P2, 00:G17 — the colour norm: `N(1 − ω) = 3` for the cube root `ω = −h + h w` of the extension at `ν = −3` (`h + h = 1`); the squared amplitude of a coloured sector, `r² = N(1 − ω) = 3`, so `Q = 1/3 + r²/6 = 5/6`.

C4.name: FRC.Flavour.koide_five_sixths
C4.doc: 28:C4, 28:X2, 28:P2 — the up-quark Koide value: `Q = 5/6 ⟺ ρ² = 3/4`, that is `6 Σ a_j² = 5 â₀²` exactly when `4 â₁ â₂ = 3 â₀²` (beside `koide_two_thirds`, `Q = 2/3 ⟺ 2 â₁ â₂ = â₀²`); with `â₁ â₂ = N(b)` and `r² = 4N(b)/a²` this is `r² = 3`, the colour norm.

C4.name: FRC.Flavour.koide_five_sixths_quadratic
C4.doc: 28:C4, 28:X2, 28:P2 — the up-quark value as a quadratic. On the amplitudes `(1, a, e)`, with `a² = m_c/m_t` and `e² = m_u/m_t`, the relation `6 Σx² = 5 (Σx)²`, that is `Q = 5/6`, is the quadratic `a² − 10 a (1 + e) + (1 + e² − 10 e) = 0`.

C4.name: FRC.Flavour.koide_up_band
C4.doc: 28:C4, 28:X2, 28:P2 — the up-quark Koide value in three schemes (`FlavourML.koide_up_band`).

C5.name: FRC.Flavour.trace_double
C5.doc: 28:C5, 00:G17 — the trace of the square of a unit: for `z z̄ = 1`, `z² + z̄² = (z + z̄)² − 2`; with `z = e^{iθ}` this is `2cos 2θ = (2cos θ)² − 2`. The lock `δ_d = δ₀/2` of 28:C5 is this relation between the cube invariants `c = cos 3δ` of the lepton and down sectors: `c_ℓ = 2 c_d² − 1`.

C5.name: FRC.Flavour.trace_triple
C5.doc: 28:C5, 00:G17 — the trace of the cube of a unit: for `z z̄ = 1`, `z³ + z̄³ = (z + z̄)³ − 3(z + z̄)`; with `z = e^{iθ}`, `2cos 3θ = (2cos θ)³ − 3(2cos θ)`. The lock `δ_u = δ₀/3` of 28:C5 is `c_ℓ = 4 c_u³ − 3 c_u` between the lepton and up cube invariants.

C5.name: FRC.Flavour.circ_det
C5.doc: 28:C1, 28:C5, 28:T1 — the determinant of a circulant: `det (circ a b c) = a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc`; at `c = b̄` this is the cube invariant `∏ √m_k = a³ + 2 Re(b³) − 3a N(b)`, whose phase part `Re(b³)` carries the phase of the sector (28:T1).

C6.name: FRC.Flavour.gst_relation
C6.doc: 28:C6, 28:X4, 28:P3 — the Gatto–Sartori–Tonin relation. A symmetric two-by-two texture `R D Rᵀ` with `R` the rotation `(c, −s; s, c)`, `c² + s² = 1`, and `D = diag(m₁, m₂)` has the `(1,1)` entry `m₁ c² + m₂ s²`; when that entry vanishes (the texture zero), `m₂ s² = −m₁ c²`, that is `tan²θ = −m₁/m₂`: the Cabibbo angle from the two light masses.

C6.name: FRC.Flavour.cabibbo_modulus
C6.doc: 28:C6, 28:X4, 28:P3 — the full Cabibbo relation: for a unit `z` (`z z̄ = 1`, the relative winding phase `e^{iφ}`) the modulus `|s_d c_u − c_d s_u z|² = s_d² c_u² + c_d² s_u² − s_d c_u c_d s_u T(z)` with `T(z) = z + z̄ = 2 cos φ`; with `s_d = √(m_d/m_s)` and `s_u = √(m_u/m_c)` this is `V_us = |√(m_d/m_s) − e^{iφ} √(m_u/m_c)|`.

C6.name: FRC.Flavour.gatto_leading
C6.doc: 28:C6, 28:X4, 28:P3 — the Gatto relation's leading term and its value at φ = π/2 (`FlavourML.gatto_leading`).

C7.name: FRC.Flavour.texture_exponents
C7.doc: 28:C7, 28:X3, 28:X6, 00:G17 — the role depths `(2, 1, 0)` as flavour charges: the down and lepton masses carry the exponents `2n = (4, 2, 0)` (the charge-carrying `10` enters once), the up masses `4n = (8, 4, 0) = 2 · (4, 2, 0)` (the `10 · 10` Yukawa enters it twice), and every exponent matrix `n_i + n_j` is symmetric.

C7.name: FRC.Flavour.texture_powers
C7.doc: 28:C7, 28:X3, 28:X6 — the effective Froggatt–Nielsen powers inside their integer brackets (`FlavourML.texture_powers`).

C8.name: FRC.Flavour.transpose_exchanges
C8.doc: 28:C8, 28:X8 — the lopsided split: `(L D Rᵀ)ᵀ = R D Lᵀ` for a diagonal `D`. A mass matrix `M_d = L D Rᵀ` whose large off-diagonal entry sits in the right-handed rotation `R` (invisible to the quark mixing, which sees `L`) has the transpose `M_e = M_dᵀ = R D Lᵀ`, where the same rotation is the left-handed one the lepton mixing sees.

C10.name: FRC.Flavour.protected_column
C10.doc: 28:C10, 28:P8 — the protected column. The shift `P` fixes the democratic vector `(1, 1, 1)`, the trivial `C₃` character; it fixes no multiple of `(2, −1, −1)` (the reducible TM1 column): `P (2, −1, −1) = (−1, −1, 2)`, and `(−1, −1, 2) = l · (2, −1, −1)` forces `−1 = 1 + 1`, that is `3 = 0`. So a `C₃` residual selects TM2.

C10.name: FRC.Flavour.trimaximal
C10.doc: 28:C10, 28:X10, 28:P8, 00:G17 — the magic matrix is trimaximal: `N(ω) = 1` and `N(ω²) = 1` for the cube root `ω = −h + h w` at `ν = −3`, so every entry `ω^{jk}/√3` of the Fourier matrix has squared modulus `1/3`.

C10.name: FRC.Flavour.jarlskog_sq
C10.doc: 28:C10, 28:X10, 28:P8, 00:G17 — the maximal Jarlskog invariant as a framed rational. The magic matrix's rephasing invariant is `F₀₀ F₁₁ F̄₀₁ F̄₁₀ = ω/9`, so `J = Im(ω)/9` and `J² = (Im ω)²/81` with `(Im ω)² = −ν h²` (the `w`-part `h` of `ω = −h + h w`, `w² = ν = −3`). Then `108 J² = 1` reads `4(−ν h²) = 3`, exact on every shell with `h + h = 1`, `ν + 3 = 0`: the continuum `J = 1/(6√3)`, `J² = 1/108`.

C10.name: FRC.Flavour.tm2_at_maximal
C10.doc: 28:C10, 28:P8 — the TM2 relation at maximal atmospheric mixing (`FlavourML.tm2_at_maximal`).

C11.name: FRC.Flavour.circ_mul
C11.doc: 28:C11 — circulants are closed under the product: `circ a b c · circ a' b' c' = circ (aa' + bc' + cb') (ab' + ba' + cc') (ac' + bb' + ca')`.

C11.name: FRC.Flavour.circ_adj
C11.doc: 28:C11 — the adjugate of a circulant is a circulant: `adj (circ a b c) = circ (a² − bc) (c² − ab) (b² − ac)`.

C11.name: FRC.Flavour.circ_transpose
C11.doc: 28:C11, 28:P5 — the transpose of a circulant is the circulant of the reversed row: `(circ a b c)ᵀ = circ a c b`.

C11.name: FRC.Flavour.seesaw_circulant
C11.doc: 28:C11, 28:X11, 00:G15 — the seesaw of circulants is circulant: `m_D · adj(M_R) · m_Dᵀ` is a circulant whenever `m_D` and `M_R` are (the inverse `M_R⁻¹ = adj(M_R)/det M_R` differs from the adjugate by the scalar), so the light neutrinos are Koide-form.

C11.name: FRC.Flavour.symmetric_circulant_spectrum
C11.doc: 28:C11 — the spectrum of a symmetric circulant. On a cube root `ω` the circulant `circ a b b` has the eigenvalues `a + 2b`, `a − b` and `a − b`: two of the three are equal. A seesaw of circulants with a symmetric Majorana matrix therefore gives two equal masses.

C11.name: FRC.Flavour.transpose_fixed_point
C11.doc: 28:C11, 28:X11, 28:P5, 00:G15 — the transpose fixed point. With `M_R = c · m_D` (the `126` alignment, 28:Y1) the seesaw collapses: `m_D · adj(c m_D) · m_Dᵀ = c² det(m_D) · m_Dᵀ`, a scalar multiple of the transpose, so the light neutrinos carry the Dirac eigenvalues (`circ_transpose`, `circ_eigen`: the transpose circulant has the eigenvalues `λ_{-k}`), the amplitude `r_ν = r_D` and the Koide value `Q_ν = Q_D = 2/3` of the colourless Dirac mass.

C11b.name: FRC.Flavour.eigen_sumsq
C11b.doc: 28:C1, 28:C2, 28:C11b, 28:X11, 28:P5 — the squares of the eigenvalues sum to `3a² + 6bc`: at `c = b̄` this is `3a² + 6 N(b)`, so `Q = Σλ²/(Σλ)² = 1/3 + (2/3) N(b)/a²`, the Koide form with `ρ² = N(b)/a²` (`koide_parseval`).

C12.name: FRC.Interactions.reflection_algebra
C12.doc: 00:G12, 28:C12 — the reflection algebra of four directions: the `16` basis elements `e_S`, `S ⊆ {0, 1, 2, 3}`, close under the product; the product is associative on the basis; distinct directions anticommute, `e_i e_j = −e_j e_i`, and each squares to zero.

C12.name: FRC.Interactions.fifth_direction
C12.doc: 00:G12, 27:C9, 28:C12 — the quarter-turn as the fifth direction maps the sixteen `e_S` of four directions one-to-one onto the sixteen even subsets of five directions, the chiral spinor `16`; for `|S|` odd the image is the product `e_S e_4` with sign `+1`.

X1.name: FRC.Interactions.koide_parseval
X1.doc: 00:G16, 27:X10, 27:P8, 28:C1, 28:X1 — Parseval on the cube-root orbit `C₃`: for amplitudes `a₀, a₁, a₂` and `ω` with `ω² + ω + 1 = 0`, `3 Σ a_j² = â₀² + 2 â₁ â₂`, `â₀ = Σ a_j`, `â₁ = a₀ + a₁ω + a₂ω²`, `â₂ = a₀ + a₁ω² + a₂ω` — the Koide form `Q = Σ a_j² / (Σ a_j)² = 1/3 + (2/3)ρ²` with `ρ² = â₁â₂/â₀²`, exact on every shell carrying the root `ω`.

X1.name: FRC.Interactions.koide_extension
X1.doc: 00:G16, 27:X10, 27:P8, 28:C2, 28:X1, 28:P1, on every shell: with `h + h = 1` and `ν = −3`, `ω = −h + h w` has `ω² + ω + 1 = 0`; `â₂ = â̄₁`, so `â₁ â₂ = N(â₁)`; Parseval `3 Σ a_j² = â₀² + 2 N(â₁)`; and `Q = 2/3 ⟺ 2 N(â₁) = â₀²` (`ρ² = 1/2`).

X1.name: FRC.Interactions.koide_half
X1.doc: 00:G16, 27:X10, 27:P8, 28:X1 — the hypotheses of `koide_extension` hold on every frame `p = 4κ + 1`, the Carrier included: `h = 2κ + 1` has `h + h = 1`, and `ν = −3` has `ν + 3 = 0`.

X3.name: FRC.Ladder.tower_reduces

X11.doc: 28:P6, 28:X11 — the brackets of the neutrino floor in micro-electronvolts: `8654² < 74 900 000 < 8655²` and `50129² < 2 513 000 000 < 50130²` for the splittings `7.49 × 10⁻⁵` and `2.513 × 10⁻³` eV², so the sum of the two masses lies between `58.783` and `58.785` meV.

P3.name: FRC.Flavour.cabibbo_modulus
P3.doc: 28:C6, 28:X4, 28:P3 — the full Cabibbo relation: for a unit `z` (`z z̄ = 1`, the relative winding phase `e^{iφ}`) the modulus `|s_d c_u − c_d s_u z|² = s_d² c_u² + c_d² s_u² − s_d c_u c_d s_u T(z)` with `T(z) = z + z̄ = 2 cos φ`; with `s_d = √(m_d/m_s)` and `s_u = √(m_u/m_c)` this is `V_us = |√(m_d/m_s) − e^{iφ} √(m_u/m_c)|`.

P3.name: FRC.Flavour.gst_relation
P3.doc: 28:C6, 28:X4, 28:P3 — the Gatto–Sartori–Tonin relation. A symmetric two-by-two texture `R D Rᵀ` with `R` the rotation `(c, −s; s, c)`, `c² + s² = 1`, and `D = diag(m₁, m₂)` has the `(1,1)` entry `m₁ c² + m₂ s²`; when that entry vanishes (the texture zero), `m₂ s² = −m₁ c²`, that is `tan²θ = −m₁/m₂`: the Cabibbo angle from the two light masses.

P3.name: FRC.Flavour.gatto_leading
P3.doc: 28:C6, 28:X4, 28:P3 — the Gatto relation's leading term and its value at φ = π/2 (`FlavourML.gatto_leading`).

P5.name: FRC.Flavour.eigen_sumsq
P5.doc: 28:C1, 28:C2, 28:C11b, 28:X11, 28:P5 — the squares of the eigenvalues sum to `3a² + 6bc`: at `c = b̄` this is `3a² + 6 N(b)`, so `Q = Σλ²/(Σλ)² = 1/3 + (2/3) N(b)/a²`, the Koide form with `ρ² = N(b)/a²` (`koide_parseval`).

P5.name: FRC.Flavour.neutrino_floor
P5.doc: 28:P5, 28:P6, 28:X11, 00:P3 — the m₁ = 0 floor of the neutrino mass sum (`FlavourML.neutrino_floor`).

P6.name: FRC.Flavour.neutrino_floor_brackets
P6.doc: 28:P6, 28:X11 — the brackets of the neutrino floor in micro-electronvolts: `8654² < 74 900 000 < 8655²` and `50129² < 2 513 000 000 < 50130²` for the splittings `7.49 × 10⁻⁵` and `2.513 × 10⁻³` eV², so the sum of the two masses lies between `58.783` and `58.785` meV.

P6.name: FRC.Flavour.neutrino_floor
P6.doc: 28:P5, 28:P6, 28:X11, 00:P3 — the m₁ = 0 floor of the neutrino mass sum (`FlavourML.neutrino_floor`).

P7.name: FRC.Flavour.majorana_brackets
P7.doc: 28:P7 — the brackets of the effective Majorana mass at `m₁ = 0`, in units of `10⁻¹¹` eV: with `s₁₂² = 0.307`, `s₁₃² = 0.02215` and the brackets of `neutrino_floor_brackets`, the difference of the two terms exceeds `1.47` meV and their sum stays below `3.71` meV.

P7.name: FRC.Flavour.majorana_band
P7.doc: 28:P7 — the effective Majorana mass band at m₁ = 0 (`FlavourML.majorana_band`).

P8.name: FRC.Flavour.protected_column
P8.doc: 28:C10, 28:P8 — the protected column. The shift `P` fixes the democratic vector `(1, 1, 1)`, the trivial `C₃` character; it fixes no multiple of `(2, −1, −1)` (the reducible TM1 column): `P (2, −1, −1) = (−1, −1, 2)`, and `(−1, −1, 2) = l · (2, −1, −1)` forces `−1 = 1 + 1`, that is `3 = 0`. So a `C₃` residual selects TM2.

P8.name: FRC.Flavour.trimaximal
P8.doc: 28:C10, 28:X10, 28:P8, 00:G17 — the magic matrix is trimaximal: `N(ω) = 1` and `N(ω²) = 1` for the cube root `ω = −h + h w` at `ν = −3`, so every entry `ω^{jk}/√3` of the Fourier matrix has squared modulus `1/3`.
